bottles.name: Raventós i Blanc de Nit Rosé
bottles.summary: Pale, dry Catalan sparkling rosé from the family that invented Cava — traditional-method, saline, food-driven bubbles to upgrade the by-the-glass brut.
bottles.profile: Very pale salmon-pink, traditional-method bubbles with red apple, blood orange, white cherry and a saline, herb-edged snap. Dry (Extra Brut) with a fine, creamy mousse and a tiny grippy texture that makes it a proper food sparkler, not a sweet aperitif.
bottles.tenSecond: Dry Spanish sparkling rosé from the family that invented Cava — pale, saline, and built for oysters, crudo, and salty-fresh plates.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid plus fine bubbles scrub salt and fat off the palate, and the saline, faintly grippy character mirrors brine — so raw shellfish, crudo, and fried snacks taste cleaner and brighter with every sip.
bottles.respell: rah-ven-TOHS ee BLAHNK deh NEET roh-ZAY
bottles.mnemonic: 'de Nit' = 'of the night' — picked before dawn so the Monastrell tints it just barely pink.
flags: GRAPE LABELLING: Menu prints 'Monastrell' but the de Nit Rosé is Xarel·lo-dominant — the 2023 release is ~49% Xarel·lo / 34% Macabeu / 9% Parellada / 7% Monastrell. Kept menu's 'Monastrell' as the grape field; staff should know the real blend if asked.
VINTAGE: Menu prints no vintage; cuvée is released by vintage year (currently 2022/2023). Set NV to match the menu — confirm the current bottle's vintage on the label.
SWEETNESS: Labelled Extra Brut (~4 g/L RS); firmly dry. Technically Extra Brut, not just Brut.
REGION/DO: NOT labelled Cava — Raventós left the Cava DO in 2012 and bottles under its own 'Conca del Riu Anoia' appellation in Penedès. Menu misspells it 'Anioa'; correct spelling is 'Anoia'.
CLIMATE: Sea-moderated Mediterranean; kept 'moderate' but a stricter reading could call summers 'warm' — defensible either way, low-stakes.

sources.note: Producer: Xarel·lo-dominant blend, Extra Brut, traditional method, Conca del Riu Anoia (left Cava DO 2012).
Importer: ~4 g/L Extra Brut; native grapes Macabeo/Xarel·lo/Parellada plus Monastrell for color.

bottles.name: Cirelli Frizzante Bianco
bottles.summary: Dry, organic Trebbiano frizzante from Abruzzo — light, citrusy, low-key ancestral-method bubbles for an easy aperitivo or seafood start.
bottles.profile: Pale straw with a soft, fine frizzante fizz. Lemon, green apple and a touch of peach with herbal/floral lift, lively acidity and a clean, dry, lightly mineral finish. Lighter and gentler than Champagne — a relaxed, low-alcohol (~10.5%) sparkler.
bottles.tenSecond: Dry organic Italian bubbles — light, citrusy, and easy; my low-key aperitivo and seafood-starter pour.
bottles.pairWhy: Light body and high acid with a gentle fizz refresh the palate without overpowering delicate food — so it lifts briny seafood, fried snacks and creamy cheese instead of competing with them.
bottles.mnemonic: Frizzante = lightly fizzy — a gentle, easy bubble, softer than full Champagne sparkle.
flags: METHOD CORRECTED: SAQ + importer (Lebendige Weine) describe Cirelli's frizzante as a NATURAL/ancestral (pét-nat, col fondo) sparkling, NOT charmat/autoclave. Confirm the exact bottle the bar pours.
SWEETNESS confirmed dry: SAQ lists sugar <1.2 g/L (drier than Brut).
STRUCTURE confirmed: 10.5% abv, light body, dominant acidity, citrus/green apple/saline (SAQ).
CLIMATE: Abruzzo is broadly warm-Mediterranean, cooled by Adriatic breezes and Apennine altitude. 'warm' explains ripeness; a case exists for 'moderate'.
VINTAGE: Menu prints no vintage; sold NV — confirm on label.
VEGAN: Estate certified organic/biodynamic and menu marks it 'v'; set vegan true per the menu marking.

sources.note: SAQ listing: ancestral/pét-nat method, sugar <1.2 g/L, 10.5% abv, citrus/saline, light body.

bottles.name: Griesel Blanc de Noirs
bottles.summary: Award-winning German traditional-method Blanc de Noirs (Pinot Noir & Meunier) — crisp, brioche-y, Champagne-shaped Sekt, the serious-bubbles upgrade.
bottles.profile: A white sparkling made from red grapes (Pinot Noir & Meunier), traditional-method with 20+ months on the lees. Brioche, white bread crust, ripe pear, apple and walnut with a whisper of red fruit; powerful yet crisp, fine mousse, mineral salinity and a dry, racy Brut finish.
bottles.tenSecond: Germany's answer to grower Champagne — Pinot Noir and Meunier, traditional-method, crisp and brioche-y. The serious-bubbles bottle.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and a fine, scrubbing mousse cut through salt and fat, while the lees-driven brioche weight and medium body give it enough presence to stand up to richer plates — so it works from oysters to fried chicken and creamy cheese.
bottles.mnemonic: Blanc de Noirs = 'white from blacks' — white wine pressed pale from red Pinot grapes.
flags: DOSAGE/SWEETNESS: Confirmed traditional-bottle-fermented Brut with very low dosage (~2 g/L); 'dry' is solidly accurate.
CLIMATE: Hessische Bergstraße is the mildest German region but still cool-climate by global standards. 'cool' correct for sparkling base.
VINTAGE: 2021 confirmed (Falstaff 93 pts). Disgorged ~March 2024 after 19+ months sur lattes.
VEGAN: Bottled unfined/unfiltered and menu marks it 'v'; set vegan true per the menu marking.

sources.note: Falstaff 93 pts 2021 Tradition Blanc de Noirs Brut; Pinot Noir & Meunier, Hessische Bergstraße, traditional method, 20+ months lees, low dosage.

bottles.name: Christophe Mignon ADN de Meunier Brut Nature
bottles.summary: Grower Champagne, 100% Pinot Meunier, zero-dosage — bone-dry, mineral and savoury; the top-of-list bubbles for purists.
bottles.profile: A 100% Pinot Meunier grower Champagne with zero dosage, so it is bone-dry and laser-focused. Red-fruit and faint floral nose; the palate is savoury and mineral — citrus confit, chamomile, dried herbs, graphite and white pepper — full-ish for a Champagne with taut, high acidity and a salty, super-dry finish.
bottles.tenSecond: Real grower Champagne, all Pinot Meunier, zero sugar — bone-dry, mineral, and savoury for the bubbles purist.
bottles.pairWhy: Bone-dry, high-acid Champagne with a fine, persistent mousse is the ultimate palate-scrubber for brine and fat, and the savoury, mineral Meunier weight lets it carry richer plates too — so it shines from raw oysters to fried snacks and creamy cheese.
bottles.respell: krees-TOFF mee-NYOHN ah-deh-EN deh muh-NYAY broot nah-TEWR
bottles.mnemonic: ADN = French for DNA — this is the 'DNA of Meunier', all one grape, nothing added (zero dosage).
flags: DOSAGE/SWEETNESS: Confirmed zero-dosage Brut Nature — bone-dry, the driest sparkler in this cohort. Jancis Robinson notes the high acidity can read as 'challenging'; set expectations as austere/savoury, not fruity-soft.
BODY: Medium-bodied for Champagne (importer: 'a bit of weight and mouthfeel'); flagged because most Champagne sits lighter.
AGING: Independently confirmed ~4 years on lees.
VINTAGE: NV cuvée blending adjacent vintages (2019/2020 and 2020/2021 bottlings) — confirm the disgorgement/base on the back label.
VEGAN: Menu marks it 'v'. Producer farms biodynamically (uncertified); set vegan true per the menu marking.
ORGANIC: Biodynamic/low-intervention farming is uncertified per importer notes.

sources.note: Wine.com/Polaner/Flatiron/Jancis Robinson: 100% Pinot Meunier, zero-dosage Brut Nature, Vallée de la Marne, biodynamic, NV, ~4 yrs lees.

bottles.name: Terroir Sense Fronteres Negre de Montsant
bottles.summary: Fresh, mineral Montsant Grenache — the bottle upgrade for the by-the-glass Sindicat la Figuera.
bottles.profile: Crunchy cherry and wild berry with warm spice, a hint of licorice, and a mineral, stony finish. Fresh acidity and fine, silky tannins keep it savory rather than jammy.
bottles.tenSecond: Fresh, stony Grenache from Montsant — the step up from our by-the-glass Sindicat, great with sausage, lamb, and duck.
bottles.pairWhy: Medium body, medium acid, and supple tannins handle fat and spice without bullying the plate — acid cuts richness, gentle grip frames the meat.
bottles.respell: teh-ROIR SEN-seh fron-TEH-res NEH-greh deh mon-SAHN
bottles.mnemonic: 'Sense Fronteres' = no borders; a fresher, lifted style of Garnacha (warm region, restrained winemaking) vs jammy Spanish reds.
flags: Montsant is a warm Mediterranean region; the wine is unoaked stainless so it reads medium/lifted, not jammy — climate word stays 'warm' to explain the grape, structure reflects the cool style.
Producer page states 100% Grenache for the current Negre; some US merchants describe an older ~75% Garnacha / 25% Cariñena blend — confirm the in-house bottle's blend if a guest asks.
Vegan true per menu 'v' mark; producer farms organically/natural but fining not independently confirmed.
Tasting/structure synthesized from producer + merchant notes for recent vintages, not a tasting of this exact 2023 bottle.

sources.note: Producer: Dominik Huber project, Montsant, 100% Grenache, whole-cluster, stainless/unoaked, medium body, silky red fruit, fresh acid, fine tannins.
Merchant lists older 75% Garnacha / 25% Cariñena blend — basis for the blend flag (vintage variation).
Montsant: warm Mediterranean climate with continental influence and high diurnal range; Garnacha is the leading red grape.
By-the-glass Sindicat la Figuera (Montsant Grenache, Light Reds, climate 'warm') names this as its upgrade.

bottles.name: Charlotte & Jean Baptiste Senat Amalgame
bottles.summary: Cool-styled, floral Minervois field blend led by Grenache — a pale, glou-glou light red.
bottles.grape: Grenache Noir, Grenache Gris & old Languedoc varieties (Piquepoul, Counoise, Terret)
bottles.profile: Bright, floral, and almost rose-pale — red berries, garrigue herbs, and a cool, juicy lift. Barely any tannin; built for chilling and easy drinking.
bottles.tenSecond: A pale, floral light red from the South of France — chill it slightly; it drinks like the easiest red on the list.
bottles.pairWhy: Light body and low tannin mean it never fights delicate or spiced food; fresh acid and herbal lift refresh fat and salt without weighing the plate down.
bottles.mnemonic: 'Amalgame' = a co-fermented field blend led by Grenache; pale, floral, gulpable.
flags: BLEND CORRECTION: menu prints 'Grenache Noir, Grenache Blanc & Grenache Gris,' but the producer's current Amalgame is a field blend of Grenache Noir, Grenache Gris, Piquepoul Noir, Counoise & Terret Noir (no Grenache Blanc). Composition varies by vintage — use menu wording with a guest but know it is not strictly three Grenaches.
Body recorded 'low' to fit the house 3-point scale; importer describes the wine as a 'pale red or dark rosé' (genuinely very light).
Climate 'warm' (Minervois is warm Mediterranean); the WINE is deliberately built cool/fresh, so structure reads lighter than the climate word implies.
Natural wine (unfined/unfiltered, minimal sulfur); vegan true per menu 'v', but fining not independently confirmed.

sources.note: Importer Les Caves de Pyrene: warm Minervois; field blend lightened with thinner-skinned, lower-alcohol grapes; 'pale red or dark rose,' floral, a wine of coolness.
Current Amalgame blend cited as Grenache Noir 40% / Grenache Gris 30% / Piquepoul Noir 10% / Counoise 10% / Terret Noir 10% — basis for blend correction.
Menu lines 30-32 print 'Grenache Noir, Grenache Blanc & Grenache Gris | Minervois, France 2022 | $90.'

bottles.name: Malahierba Vinos Maleza
bottles.summary: Mountain Rufete from Sierra de Salamanca — a rare, Pinot-like light red, all red fruit and high acid.
bottles.profile: High-toned cherry, pomegranate, and cranberry with wild herbs, sweet spice, and a tangy, savory finish. Thin-skinned Rufete gives soft, velvety tannins and bright, lifted acidity — think Pinot's lighter cousin.
bottles.tenSecond: A rare mountain grape from western Spain — light, red-fruited, and zippy, like a wilder Pinot Noir. Pour it for the Burgundy curious.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and feather-light tannin keep it nimble; it lifts herbs, vinaigrette, and lighter proteins instead of flattening them, and the acid scrubs fat clean.
bottles.mnemonic: Rufete = thin-skinned mountain grape = pale, high-acid, soft-tannin — Spain's answer to Pinot.
flags: Rufete is an obscure variety; structure (light body, high acid, soft tannin) is sourced from varietal references and producer notes, not a tasting of this exact bottle.
Body recorded 'low' to fit the house 3-point scale; sources call Rufete 'light' to 'light-to-medium' bodied.
Climate 'cool' reflects the high-altitude Sierra de Salamanca mountain sites; the broader region is warm interior Spain, so this is altitude-driven cool — worth saying to a guest.
Tiny production; barrel-aged (acacia) adds gentle spice not oak weight; vegan true per menu 'v' but fining not independently confirmed.

sources.note: Calgary importer Metrovino: Malahierba in Sierra de Salamanca; Maleza macerated then acacia-aged; cherry, juicy berry, sweet spice.
Rufete: thin-skinned, light-coloured, noticeable acidity, light-bodied with supple tannins; described as a Spanish version of Pinot Noir.
Wine-Searcher: Rufete (a.k.a. Tinta Pinheira), thin-skinned, light wines — confirms varietal character and spelling.

bottles.name: Alta Mora Etna Rosso
bottles.summary: High-altitude volcanic Nerello Mascalese — Sicily's Pinot-like light red, pale and high-acid.
bottles.profile: Pale ruby with red cherry, cranberry, dried rose, and pepper over a faint iron-and-salt mineral thread. Bright acidity and fine, delicate tannins — an elegant, savory Etna red.
bottles.tenSecond: Sicily's Pinot Noir — grown high on Mount Etna's volcano, so it's pale, fresh, and red-fruited, not heavy.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and fine, gentle tannin mean it slips alongside lighter meats, mushrooms, and tomato without overpowering; the savory mineral streak loves umami.
bottles.respell: AHL-tah MOH-rah, ET-nah ROH-soh, neh-REL-loh mahs-kah-LEH-zeh
bottles.mnemonic: Alta Mora = 'high' on Etna; altitude + volcano = pale, high-acid, Pinot-shaped red.
flags: Climate 'cool' explains the structure: Etna sits in warm Sicily, but vineyards at ~350-1,000 m on the volcano give cool nights, high acid, pale color, and fine tannin. Tell guests: high-altitude Sicily, not a cold region.
Tannin recorded 'medium': Nerello's tannin is firmer/more noticeable than Pinot's, so 'medium' is correct rather than 'low'.
Vegan true per menu 'v'; fining not independently confirmed.

sources.note: Wine Enthusiast on Alta Mora: red cherry/cranberry, rose, pepper, saline, bright acid, delicate tannins, medium body.
Wine Folly: Nerello Mascalese on Etna ~350-1,000 m; altitude/diurnal range preserve acidity, pale color, fine-but-firm tannin.
Alta Mora = Cusumano's Etna estate; Nerello Mascalese, large neutral oak.

bottles.name: Pierre Thibert Chorey-les-Beaune
bottles.summary: Approachable village red Burgundy — classic, lively Pinot Noir, the easy way into the Côte de Beaune.
bottles.profile: Textbook red Burgundy: raspberry and black cherry lifted by earth, forest floor, and gentle spice. Bright acidity and fine, subtle tannins make it lively and food-friendly.
bottles.tenSecond: Real red Burgundy without the Grand Cru price — fresh, earthy Pinot Noir; the friendly door into the Côte de Beaune.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and silky, restrained tannin flatter lighter proteins and mushrooms; the savory earth tone mirrors umami while the acid keeps fat in check.
bottles.mnemonic: Chorey-les-Beaune = the humble neighbor of Aloxe-Corton; honest, lively Pinot at a gentler price.
flags: No 'v' on the menu, so vegan is null (not false) — tell a vegan guest you will check; Burgundy reds are often unfined but confirm.
Climate recorded 'cool': BIVB/Berry Bros. describe a continental climate; for Burgundy Pinot, 'cool' is the house-vocabulary word that explains the high acid and pale/medium body.
Tasting/structure drawn from producer-importer notes and the appellation profile, not a tasting of the exact 2023 bottle.
Producer 'Pierre Thibert' is a small domaine; only limited merchant data — appellation character well-sourced, the specific cuvée less so.

sources.note: Importer (Elden Selections): classic Burgundy Pinot — raspberry, black cherry, earth, spice; subtle tannic structure; small family domaine.
BIVB: Chorey-les-Beaune, Côte de Beaune; continental climate, marl/limestone; generous, approachable reds, an excellent intro to Bourgogne.
Berry Bros. & Rudd: elegant, medium-bodied, early-drinking Pinot, red berry and earthy notes.

bottles.name: Sandrine & Fabrice Gasnier Chinon Pierres Chaudes
bottles.summary: Biodynamic Loire Cabernet Franc — red fruit, graphite, and silky tannin; a fresh, savory medium red.
bottles.profile: Raspberry, red currant, and cassis with graphite, garrigue herbs, and a touch of pepper. Silky tannins and fresh acidity give a medium-bodied, savory Loire Cabernet Franc.
bottles.tenSecond: Loire Cabernet Franc — bright red fruit with a leafy, peppery edge and smooth tannins. Great with herbs, charcuterie, and lamb.
bottles.pairWhy: Medium tannin and fresh acid handle herbs and gamey fat without turning harsh; the wine's own peppery, herbal streak echoes green and spiced flavors on the plate.
bottles.mnemonic: Chinon = the Loire's home of Cabernet Franc; 'Pierres Chaudes' = warm stones = riper, rounder fruit.
flags: NAME CORRECTION: menu prints 'Sandrine & Fabrice Chinon Gasnier Pierres Chaudes' (words transposed); domaine is Sandrine & Fabrice Gasnier, Chinon AOC, cuvée 'Les Pierres Chaudes' — fixed in the record name.

Acidity recorded 'medium': some Chinon references cite 'high acidity', but this riper 'Pierres Chaudes' (warm-stone) site gives rounder fruit. 'Medium' fits the riper cuvée per the SAQ note; a leaner Chinon would read higher-acid.
Climate 'moderate' fits the Loire (maritime tempering continental).
Vegan true per menu 'v'; estate is biodynamic (Demeter-style) — fining not independently confirmed.

sources.note: SAQ on Gasnier Chinon Pierres Chaudes 2022: raspberry, graphite, humus; medium body, generous mouthfeel, present acidity; clay-silica over limestone.
Chinon: Cabernet Franc, maritime-moderated continental climate; medium tannin, fresh acidity.
Menu lines 39-40 print transposed name; corrected to Gasnier domaine, 'Les Pierres Chaudes'.

bottles.name: Domaine de Colette Coteaux de Colette
bottles.summary: Old-vine Beaujolais-Villages Gamay — juicy cherry and crunchy red fruit with silky, low tannin.
bottles.profile: Juicy, crunchy red fruit — cherry, raspberry, red currant — with floral lift and a wet-stone freshness. Silky low tannin and bright acid make it the breeziest red on the list.
bottles.tenSecond: Old-vine Beaujolais Gamay — bright, juicy cherry with barely any tannin. Chill it slightly; it's everybody's easy red.
bottles.pairWhy: Low tannin and high acid mean it never clashes — it refreshes salt, fat, and charcuterie, and is light enough for poultry, salmon, and lighter plates.
bottles.respell: doh-MEN deh koh-LET, koh-TOH deh koh-LET
bottles.mnemonic: Gamay from Beaujolais = Pinot's juicy, low-tannin cousin; chillable and crowd-pleasing.
flags: Menu label is just 'Coteaux de Colette'; this is Domaine de Colette's Beaujolais-Villages cuvée, from 60+ year-old Gamay sourced in the Morgon and Régnié cru villages.
Body recorded 'low' to fit the house 3-point scale (classic light Beaujolais-Villages).
Tannin 'low' confirmed but importer says tannin is 'fully ripe and rounded' — soft, not absent; acidity gives the wine its structure.
Vegan true per menu 'v'; estate converting to organic from 2020 — fining not independently confirmed.

sources.note: Domaine de Colette: 60+ yr-old Gamay from Morgon & Régnié crus; acidity gives structure, light/ripe tannins, juicy cherry.
Wine Enthusiast: fresh, lively Gamay, red fruit and floral, light and food-friendly.

bottles.name: Castello di Verduno Alba
bottles.summary: Classic Barbera d'Alba from a historic Verduno estate — juicy dark cherry, low tannin grip, bright acid.
bottles.profile: Vivid blackberry, sour cherry, and plum with violet and a little dark spice. Barbera's signature high acid with low tannin makes it juicy, fresh, and easy-drinking.
bottles.tenSecond: Piedmont Barbera — all juicy dark cherry and zip, with almost no tannin. The crowd-pleasing red from Barolo country.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and low tannin cut through tomato, fat, and salt without any grip to fight the food — the natural partner for pizza, pasta, and sausage.
bottles.mnemonic: Barbera = high acid, low tannin = the juicy Italian pizza-and-pasta red from Barolo's backyard.
flags: Menu shortens the name to 'Castello di Verduno Alba'; with 'Barbera | Piedmont' this is the estate's Barbera d'Alba. Not the estate's 'Basadone' Pelaverga.
Climate 'moderate' explains Barbera's classic high-acid / low-tannin profile from northern Piedmont.
Vegan true per menu 'v'; fining not independently confirmed.

sources.note: Merchant on the 2024 Castello di Verduno Barbera d'Alba: vivid blackberry/sour cherry/plum, violet, bright acidity, silky energetic palate.
Barbera: deep ruby, low tannin, bracing high acidity, juicy fruit.
Castello di Verduno (historic Verduno estate, northern edge of Barolo) makes a Barbera d'Alba; menu's 'Alba' + 'Barbera' = this wine, distinct from its Pelaverga.

bottles.name: Brandini Langhe Filari Corti
bottles.summary: Approachable La Morra Nebbiolo — rose, red cherry and tar with the high-acid, firm-but-silky tannin of Piedmont.
bottles.profile: Perfumed rose, violet and red cherry with classic licorice and tar on the finish. High acid and firm but silky tannins make it elegant rather than heavy — the gateway Nebbiolo.
bottles.tenSecond: The classy Italian red — rose and red cherry with grippy tannin and bright acid, made for truffle, mushroom and rich pasta.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and firm tannin cut through fat and umami: the acid refreshes against duck and mushroom, the tannin grips meaty richness without overwhelming the wine's perfume.
bottles.mnemonic: Nebbiolo = nebbia = fog; pale colour, big perfume, firm grip.
flags: Climate 'moderate' confirmed: La Morra/Langhe is continental (cold snowy winters, hot summers, autumn fog) with a wide diurnal swing that drives the high acid + aromatics — not 'warm'.
Structure confirmed: producer and Wine Folly describe fresh/lively acidity, silky-but-firm tannin from La Morra's sandy soils — textbook Nebbiolo.

Family/upgradeFrom tension: family='Structured Reds' (correct for high-tannin Nebbiolo) but upgradeFrom='Light reds'. Defensible as the gateway/approachable Nebbiolo upgrading the by-the-glass Nebbiolo lane; flag for menu-owner review of lane consistency.
Vegan: not marked 'v' on the menu, so vegan=null is correct — confirm fining before serving a vegan guest.

sources.note: Wine Folly + producer/retailers: La Morra continental/diurnal climate; Nebbiolo high acid, firm-but-silky tannin, rose/cherry/tar.

bottles.name: Kistler
bottles.summary: Benchmark Russian River Pinot Noir — ripe black cherry and spice, plush yet structured with velvety tannin and bright acid.
bottles.region: Russian River Valley, Sonoma County, California, USA
bottles.profile: Ripe black cherry, raspberry and violet layered with clove, cola and forest floor. Plush and seamless on the palate but kept lively by bright acidity and velvety tannin — the splurge Pinot.
bottles.tenSecond: The special-occasion California Pinot — silky black cherry and spice, elegant enough for duck, salmon and mushrooms.
bottles.pairWhy: Medium body and supple tannin slot under lighter proteins, while the bright acidity lifts fatty fish and rich poultry without overpowering — Pinot's classic crowd-pleasing middle ground.
bottles.mnemonic: Kistler — famous for Chardonnay, here a plush splurge Pinot.
flags: Climate 'moderate' confirmed: Russian River has warm afternoons but cool maritime fog; slow even ripening gives ripe fruit with retained acidity — fog, not heat, drives the structure.

Structure confirmed: 2022 Kistler RRV Pinot described as medium-bodied, bright/medium-high acidity, medium plush tannins. Body 'medium' may read fuller than a lean Burgundy; flag for a guest expecting featherweight Pinot.
Vegan=true accepted on the menu's 'v' mark; house rule treats the menu mark as confirmation.

sources.note: Producer + critics: Russian River cool-fog climate; 2022 medium body, bright acid, medium tannin.

bottles.name: Castello di Potentino Sacromonte
bottles.summary: High-altitude volcanic Sangiovese from Monte Amiata — fresh, mineral and brambly with raspy tannin, unlike warm Chianti.
bottles.profile: Brambly red and black berry, garden herbs and sweet blossom over a stony, mineral core, with nervy raspy tannins and a tangy finish. A fresher, higher-altitude take on Sangiovese than Chianti.
bottles.tenSecond: A mineral, mountain-grown Sangiovese — fresh sour-cherry acid and herbs, the brainier cousin of the house Chianti.
bottles.pairWhy: High acidity is built for tomato and herb dishes — it matches the acid in the sauce so the wine stays lively — while medium tannin handles cured meats and grilled lamb.
bottles.mnemonic: Sacromonte = 'sacred mountain' (Monte Amiata) — volcanic, high, fresh.
flags: Climate 'moderate' confirmed: estate on the slopes of Monte Amiata (extinct volcano), high-altitude + volcanic soil distinguish it from warmer lowland Chianti — freshness/minerality, not heat.

Appellation nuance: estate sits within the Montecucco DOC area but Sacromonte is typically bottled IGT Toscana (declassified). Region 'Monte Amiata, Tuscany' asserts no specific DOC; the 'montecucco' alias is approximate, not a guaranteed label term.
Structure inferred from 'fresh, nervy raspy tannins, mineral' descriptors; no published WSET grid — taste to confirm.
2018 vintage is ~7-8 years old at service; expect some savoury/tertiary development (maturity, not a fault).
Vegan: not marked 'v'; natural/low-intervention estate but vegan status unconfirmed — confirm before serving a vegan guest.

sources.note: Producer: Monte Amiata volcanic/high-altitude, 100% Sangiovese; IGT Toscana declassified bottling.

bottles.name: Fletcher Barbaresco Recta Pete
bottles.summary: Artisan Barbaresco, 100% Nebbiolo — red cherry, rose and tar with firm dusty tannin and an amaro finish; the elegant top-Nebbiolo bottle.
bottles.profile: Bright red cherry, rose petal and dried herb over tar, iron and roasted chestnut, with firm dusty tannins and a long amaro finish. Elegant and perfumed — Barbaresco's classier, slightly softer take on Nebbiolo.
bottles.tenSecond: The serious Nebbiolo splurge — Barbaresco perfume of cherry, rose and tar with firm tannin built for truffle, duck and lamb.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and firm tannin demand fat and umami: they scrub richness from duck and lamb and resonate with earthy mushroom and truffle, while the wine's perfume survives bold dishes.
bottles.mnemonic: Fletcher = 'shoot straight'; Barbaresco = Barolo's elegant sibling.
flags: Climate 'moderate' confirmed: Barbaresco/Langhe continental climate; diurnal swing explains the high acid + firm tannin, not heat.

Structure confirmed: firm/fine persistent tannins, red cherry/rose/spice/liquorice, mineral core, amaro finish — textbook Barbaresco. Body 'medium' with high tannin: don't let a guest read the pale colour as a light wine.
'Recta Pete' = 'shoot straight' (winemaker David Fletcher); respell PEH-teh (Italianate, not English 'Pete'). Best-effort — no authoritative audio source.
Vegan=true accepted on the menu's 'v' mark; organic/biodynamic vineyards.

bottles.name: Texier Brézème
bottles.summary: Cool-leaning northern Rhône Syrah — savoury olive, black pepper and red fruit, fresh and medium-bodied rather than a fruit bomb.
bottles.profile: Red and black fruit, black olive, cured meat and cracked black pepper over a stony mineral core. Fresh, savoury and medium-bodied — northern Rhône Syrah in a peppery, almost Burgundian style, not a jammy bruiser.
bottles.tenSecond: The peppery, savoury Syrah — black olive, smoke and cracked pepper with real freshness, made for lamb, sausage and grilled meat.
bottles.pairWhy: Black-pepper and savoury olive notes echo grilled and charred meats, while the bright acidity and medium tannin keep up with fat without the wine tasting heavy or sweet.
bottles.mnemonic: Brézème = the lone northern-Rhône slope; cool, peppery Syrah.
flags: Climate: Brézème is a single limestone slope (~300m) with a COOLER microclimate giving Syrah a 'distinctly northern' fresh/savoury profile. 'moderate' is acceptable as the structural word, but the wine clearly drinks cooler/fresher than a southern Syrah — could be argued 'cool'; kept 'moderate' and flagged.
Structure confirmed: cool-climate, lighter-bodied, good acidity, subtle tannins, olive/pepper/meat.
Producer ambiguity: menu lists 'Texier' only; the 2023 Brézème rouge exists from both Éric Texier and son Martin Texier. Profile holds for either; confirm bottling if a guest asks.
Vegan: not marked 'v'; low-intervention producer but vegan status unconfirmed — confirm before serving a vegan guest.

sources.note: Producer + retailers: Brézème cool limestone slope, Côtes-du-Rhône labelling, fresh/savoury Syrah, olive/pepper/meat.

bottles.name: Algre Valgañón
bottles.summary: High, cold-village Rioja (Tempranillo & Garnacha) — floral, fresh and red-fruited, a lighter old-vine Rioja, not an oaky blockbuster.
bottles.profile: Violet and geranium florals with pink peppercorn and bright red and black fruit. From one of Rioja's highest, coldest villages, it's fresh, gentle and medium-bodied — an elegant, lighter Rioja rather than a heavy oaked Reserva.
bottles.tenSecond: The fresh, floral Rioja — bright red fruit and pink pepper from a cold mountain village, gentler than a big oaky Rioja.
bottles.pairWhy: High acidity and gentle tannin make it food-flexible: it lifts tomato and cured meats and complements roast chicken and lamb sausage without the weight of an oak-heavy red.
bottles.mnemonic: Alegre y Valgañón = the growers' names; high cold Rioja village = fresh, floral.
flags: Producer SPELLING: correct name is 'Alegre Valgañón' / 'Alegre y Valgañón' (Óscar Alegre + Eva Valgañón, est. 2010). Menu prints 'Algre Valgañon' (typo, missing 'e' and tilde) — name field carries the menu's printed form; respell/profile reflect the correct 'Alegre'.

Climate 'cool' verified high confidence: Fonzaleche (~600m, Obarenes Mountains) is one of the highest and coldest villages in Rioja, giving 'light and fluid wines with excellent acid structure'. Do NOT pitch as a warm, jammy Spanish red.

Body/tannin 'medium' inferred from 'gentle/light and fluid' descriptors; no WSET grid — genuinely on the lighter side.
Vegan=true accepted on the menu's 'v' mark; natural, low-intervention wine.

sources.note: Producer + importer: Alegre Valgañón, Fonzaleche cold high-altitude site; Tempranillo/Garnacha; light/fluid/high-acid.

bottles.name: Gulfi Nerojbleo
bottles.summary: Higher-elevation Sicilian Nero d'Avola — fresh black and red fruit, violet and spice with firm tannin and surprising minerality.
bottles.profile: Ripe blackberry and plum, crushed violet, lavender and spice over a savoury, mineral underlay. Full-bodied with muscular but fine tannins — a brighter, more structured Nero d'Avola from higher-elevation Sicilian (Hyblean Mountains) sites.
bottles.tenSecond: The big, dark Sicilian red — blackberry, violet and spice with real body and grip, made for lamb, sausage and ribeye.
bottles.pairWhy: Full body and firm tannin stand up to fatty, smoky meats, while the savoury herbal-mineral streak keeps it from tasting jammy alongside grilled lamb and sausage.
bottles.mnemonic: Nero d'Avola = 'black of Avola'; Sicily's dark, full-bodied red.
flags: BODY is genuinely contested: SAQ (2022) calls it 'full-bodied' (supports 'high'), but multiple importers/critics call it 'medium' to 'medium-full' because Gulfi's higher-elevation Hyblean fruit is fresher. Body 'high' kept as defensible for 2022 but may read medium-to-full — taste to confirm.
ACIDITY likely understated: sources note 'brisk / cooling / surging' acidity. 'medium' is the floor; medium-to-high is at least as defensible. Flagged rather than changed.
Climate 'warm' correct at regional level (Sicily is hot); the higher-elevation site explains freshness but does not make the climate cool.
Appellation: labelled Sicilia DOC / Terre Siciliane IGT depending on release — both seen.
'Nerojbleo' respell best-effort (Nero d'Avola + Jbleo/Hyblean); stress neh-roy-BLEH-oh, approximate — no authoritative audio.
Vegan=true accepted on the menu's 'v' mark; organic/biodynamic.

sources.note: SAQ (2022) 'full-bodied'; importers 'medium/brisk acidity'; higher-elevation Hyblean fruit, Sicily warm.

bottles.name: Domaine Gour de Chaulé Gigondas Les Jardinières
bottles.summary: Old-vine Gigondas (Grenache-led) — ripe red fruit, garrigue and white pepper with suave, structured tannin; the warm southern-Rhône bottle.
bottles.profile: Ripe and macerated red fruit, garrigue herbs, lavender and crushed white pepper with a minty lift. Full-bodied and suave, with dusty but supple old-vine tannins and good length — generous southern Rhône with structure.
bottles.tenSecond: The warm, generous southern-Rhône red — ripe red fruit, garrigue and spice with full body and supple grip, made for lamb and steak.
bottles.pairWhy: Ripe fruit, herb (garrigue) and full body mirror Provençal-style grilled meats; supple tannin handles the fat of lamb and ribeye while the wine stays generous rather than austere.

bottles.mnemonic: Gigondas = Châteauneuf's rugged neighbour; Grenache-led, full and warm.
flags: Climate 'warm' confirmed: Gigondas is southern Rhône Mediterranean (one of France's warmest regions); ripe fruit, garrigue and full body follow. Acidity 'medium' correct (Grenache-led, not high-acid).
Blend confirmed: ~80% Grenache / 10% Syrah / 10% Mourvèdre; menu lists 'Grenache, Syrah & Mourvèdre' — consistent. 2023 '.1871 Les Jardinières' bottling verified.
Pronounce the final 's' in Gigondas (zhee-gon-DAHSS) — common error is dropping it.

bottles.name: Château Larose Perganson
bottles.summary: Classic Haut-Médoc claret (Cabernet & Merlot) — cassis, cedar and tobacco with grippy tannin; the textbook left-bank Bordeaux bottle.
bottles.profile: Blackcurrant and red plum with cedar, tobacco, graphite and a touch of bell pepper. Medium-to-full bodied with firm, structured tannins — a classic, savoury left-bank Bordeaux built around Cabernet and Merlot.
bottles.tenSecond: The textbook Bordeaux — cassis, cedar and tobacco with firm tannin, the classic steak-and-lamb claret.
bottles.pairWhy: Firm Cabernet tannin is made for red meat: it binds with protein and fat so steak tastes smoother and the wine softens — the original reason claret and beef are paired.
bottles.mnemonic: Haut-Médoc = left-bank Bordeaux = Cabernet-led, cedar and cassis.
flags: Climate 'moderate' confirmed: Haut-Médoc/Bordeaux maritime-temperate; cedar/graphite/firm-tannin profile and medium acid reflect this climate, not warmth.
Blend confirmed as ~50/50 Cabernet Sauvignon / Merlot for 2018; Cru Bourgeois Supérieur (designated 2020). Spelling 'Château Larose Perganson, Haut-Médoc' verified.
Structure confirmed: rich/firm tannins, concentration, drink from 2024. Profile says 'medium-to-full' while grid sets body 'high' — defensible for firm left-bank claret.
Bell-pepper (pyrazine) note appears in 2018 reviews — varietal Cabernet character, not a flaw. Drinking window ~2024-2036.
Vegan: not marked 'v'; Bordeaux estates commonly use egg-white fining — confirm before serving a vegan guest, vegan=null is correct.

sources.note: Wine Enthusiast/Decanter/wine.com: 50/50 Cab/Merlot 2018, Cru Bourgeois Supérieur, firm tannin, Haut-Médoc.

bottles.name: Whitehall Lane
bottles.summary: Plush Napa Valley Merlot — ripe plum, red cherry and mocha with creamy, supple tannin; the soft, generous Napa red.
bottles.profile: Ripe plum, red cherry and mixed berry with mocha, chocolate and a touch of vanilla and licorice. Full-bodied, supple and round with fine, creamy tannins — the soft, plush, crowd-pleasing Napa red.
bottles.tenSecond: The smooth, plush Napa Merlot — ripe plum, cherry and chocolate with soft tannin; an easy, generous red for almost any table.
bottles.pairWhy: Soft, supple tannin and ripe fruit make it gentle and flexible — it flatters grilled chicken, duck and medium-weight beef without the firm grip that can fight delicate dishes.
bottles.mnemonic: Merlot = soft, plush, plummy; Napa = ripe and full.
flags: Climate 'warm' confirmed: Napa Valley warm Mediterranean; ripe plush fruit and full body follow. Tannin 'medium' confirmed — fine/juicy/creamy/supple, softer than Cabernet (key contrast for the Napa-Merlot translator answer).
Body 'high': sources say 'medium-to-full bodied, plush, round, succulent' — body 'high' is the upper end of that; defensible.
Grape: menu lists simply 'Merlot'; the actual bottling is Merlot-dominant (~82% Merlot with small Cab/Malbec/PV/Cab Franc). Single-grape 'Merlot' is correct as a menu-driven simplification.
Vegan: not marked 'v' — vegan=null correct; confirm fining before serving a vegan guest.
This is one of the two Napa Merlot/Cab translator answers (Merlot = soft/plush vs White Rock's firmer Cabernet).

sources.note: Producer + critics: 2021 Napa Merlot plush/supple, medium tannin, full body, Merlot-dominant blend.

bottles.name: Aia Vecchia Sor Ugo Bolgheri Superiore
bottles.summary: Coastal Tuscan Bordeaux blend (Cab/Merlot/Cab Franc) — cherry, plum, menthol and herbs with dusty tannin; a polished Super Tuscan.
bottles.profile: Ripe dark cherry, plum and blueberry with menthol, rosemary, licorice and a hint of chocolate and incense. Full-bodied and round with plenty of dusty tannin and ripe acidity — a polished coastal Tuscan Super Tuscan in the Bordeaux mould.
bottles.tenSecond: The Super Tuscan — coastal Tuscan Cabernet-Merlot with dark cherry, herbs and dusty tannin, the Italian answer to a Napa or Bordeaux red.
bottles.pairWhy: Full body and firm dusty tannin are built for red meat — they cut the fat of ribeye and lamb — while the menthol-herb lift keeps the rich wine from tasting heavy.

bottles.name: White Rock
bottles.summary: Estate Stags-Leap-foothills Napa Cabernet — dark plum, blackberry, cedar and tobacco; concentrated but balanced and restrained for Napa.

bottles.profile: Dark plum, blackberry and bramble with leather, old cedar, tobacco spice and roasted coffee. Full-bodied and concentrated from old-vine volcanic-ash soils, but balanced and refined rather than an over-ripe fruit bomb — the structured, age-worthy Napa Cabernet.
bottles.tenSecond: The serious estate Napa Cabernet — dark berry, cedar and coffee with firm tannin and real structure, the top steak red on the list.
bottles.pairWhy: Firm, full Cabernet tannin is built for the fattiest beef — ribeye and steak — binding protein and fat so both wine and meat taste smoother; the savoury cedar/tobacco notes echo the char.
bottles.mnemonic: White Rock = white volcanic ash soils at the foot of Stags Leap; structured Napa Cab.
flags: Climate 'warm' confirmed: Napa Valley warm Mediterranean; full body, ripe dark fruit follow. Estate described as 'balanced/seamless' with 'grainy tannins, drying chalky character' — supports the 'balanced and refined' framing and the firmer counterpart to Whitehall Lane Merlot in the Napa Cab/Merlot translator.

sources.note: Producer + Napa Valley Life + napawineproject: 2019 estate Cabernet, Stags-Leap-foothills volcanic ash, warm climate, firm tannin.

bottles.name: Denizot Sancerre
bottles.summary: The classic Loire Sauvignon Blanc — cool, flinty, grapefruit-crisp — the premium step up from the by-the-glass crisp whites.
bottles.profile: Grapefruit, lime, gooseberry, and a chalky, flinty snap from Sancerre's limestone soils. Bone-dry and tightly focused with a long mineral finish.
bottles.tenSecond: The benchmark crisp white — flinty Loire Sauvignon Blanc, bone-dry and built for oysters and goat cheese.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and zero sweetness cut through brine, fat, and fried batter, while the citrus echoes lemon-dressed seafood and greens — it refreshes the palate instead of competing with delicate plates.

bottles.name: Donnhoff Feinherb

bottles.name: Maloof Where Ya Pjs At?
bottles.summary: Willamette skin-contact orange wine led by Pinot Gris — gentle grip, bright acid, super food-friendly.
bottles.profile: An orange wine: skin-contact Pinot Gris brings soft herbs, dried apricot and a light cherry-candy note with a gentle savory grip, lifted by high-toned acidity, with barrel-fermented Riesling in the blend. Dry, unfined and unfiltered.
bottles.tenSecond: This is our orange wine — skin-contact Pinot Gris from Oregon. A little grippy and savory, super dry, and a brilliant bridge between white and red for charcuterie and grilled dishes.
bottles.pairWhy: Skin-contact gives a light tannic grip and savory texture that stands up to spice, fat and char, while the high acid keeps it refreshing — so it handles dishes a normal white can't.
bottles.mnemonic: PJs = cozy, casual, fun = the easygoing orange wine.
flags: Blend varies by source: multiple retailers give 2022 as ~80% skin-contact Pinot Gris / 20% Riesling; the winery adds small 'odds and ends' (Gewürz, Müller-Thurgau, etc.). Menu labels it 'Skin Contact Pinot Gris' — kept Pinot Gris as the lead grape.
It is an orange/skin-contact wine, not a conventional white — 'tannin: low' reflects the light skin-contact grip. Set guest expectations: savory and lightly grippy, not crisp-and-clean.
Sweetness is dry but the cherry-candy aroma can read 'fruity' to guests — taste-confirm if someone is sugar-averse.
Profile edited: removed the assertion that the high acid comes specifically 'from barrel-fermented Riesling' — reworded to keep barrel-fermented Riesling as a blend fact only.

sources.note: Producer: skin-contact Pinot Gris-led blend, neutral-oak fermentation, natural / unfined-unfiltered.
2022 Willamette Pinot Gris & Riesling, skin-contact; ~80/20 PG/Riesling, gris on skins ~21 days, neutral oak.

bottles.name: Clos Bellane Valréas
bottles.summary: High-altitude southern Rhône white blend — floral and full but kept fresh by 400m limestone slopes.
bottles.region: Côtes du Rhône Villages Valréas, Rhône Valley
bottles.profile: A southern-Rhône white led by Marsanne with Viognier lift — white peach, citrus, white flowers and honeysuckle over a stony, mineral finish. The 400m limestone altitude keeps an otherwise sunny site fresh and balanced rather than heavy.
bottles.tenSecond: A floral, gently full white from the high slopes of the southern Rhône — peach and white flowers with real freshness. Lovely with roast chicken, squash, and creamy plates.
bottles.pairWhy: Medium body and a round, aromatic mouthfeel match richer vegetable and poultry dishes, while the altitude-driven freshness keeps it from feeling flat against fat or spice.
bottles.mnemonic: Bellane on the high 'plateau' = altitude = a Rhône white that stays fresh.
flags: Acidity called medium: the 400m site gives more freshness than a typical southern-Rhône white, but Marsanne-led blends are not high-acid — medium is the honest WSET call.

Climate 'moderate' is a judgment call: the southern Rhône is warm, but 400m limestone altitude tempers it and an importer describes the site as cool/high-altitude — 'moderate' captures the net effect.
Not marked 'v' on the menu, so vegan is null; estate is organic/biodynamic but that does not guarantee vegan fining — defer to confirmation.
Blend proportions (Marsanne ~65% / Viognier ~30% / Roussanne ~5%) are from the estate/importer and can shift slightly by vintage.

sources.note: Stéphane Vedeau, ~400m elevation, active limestone soils, biodynamic; Marsanne/Roussanne/Viognier blend.
Wine-Searcher + Vins Rhône official confirm 'Valréas', a Côtes du Rhône Villages enclave in Vaucluse.

bottles.pairWhy: Lees-built texture and medium body wrap around butter, cream and roasted flavours, while the pithy dry acidity stops it turning heavy — a natural match for richer fish and poultry.

translatorRows.phrase: If you love Beaujolais for that light, juicy, low-tannin red, the Deinhard Pinot is the same easy lane by the glass — and if you want the real Gamay, the Domaine de Colette is exactly that, straight from Beaujolais.
flags: By-the-glass match (Pinot Noir) is the same structural lane, not the same grape; the true Gamay is bottle-only (Domaine de Colette).
Deinhard Deidesheim is Pfalz Pinot Noir — Pfalz is the warmest/sunniest German region, so it leans fruitier and rounder than a textbook cool-climate Pinot, but still light and low-tannin.

sources.note: Beaujolais = Gamay; Domaine de Colette is Beaujolais-Villages (Gamay).
Gamay: light-to-medium body, low tannin, high/lively acidity, red cherry/raspberry/strawberry.

translatorRows.name: Viognier / white Rhône
translatorRows.summary: No Viognier by the glass; the round Spanish Chardonnay carries the weight, and the Clos Bellane Valréas bottle is a true white Rhône with Viognier in the blend.
translatorRows.familiar: A fuller, rounder white with weight and texture rather than sharp zip — ripe stone fruit and citrus that handle trout, cod, crab, and creamy or buttery plates.
translatorRows.different: By the glass it is Spanish Chardonnay, so you get the body but not Viognier's perfumed, peachy aromatics. The Clos Bellane bottle is the real white Rhône — Marsanne, Viognier and Roussanne blended.
translatorRows.phrase: There is no Viognier by the glass, but if it is the rounder, fuller white you want, the Spanish Chardonnay delivers that weight — and for the genuine white Rhône, the Clos Bellane Valréas is a Marsanne-Viognier-Roussanne blend.
flags: No Viognier-based wine by the glass; closest glass (Chardonnay) shares body/texture but not Viognier's aromatics. True match is bottle-only (Clos Bellane, a Marsanne-Viognier-Roussanne blend, not 100% Viognier).
Menu spells the bottle 'Clos Bellane Valreas'; correct accented spelling is 'Valréas' — cosmetic only.

sources.note: Menu line 110-111: Clos Bellane Valréas = Marsanne, Viognier & Roussanne | Rhône Valley 2023.
Viognier/white Rhône is a fuller-bodied, perfumed/peachy white.

translatorRows.name: Gewürztraminer / aromatic white
translatorRows.summary: No Gewürz on the list; the off-dry Darting Riesling is the honest aromatic, fruit-forward stand-in.
translatorRows.familiar: Perfumed, fruit-forward white with peach and lime lift and a touch of off-dry softness — aromatic and friendly, and a strong partner for spice, chili, honey, and pickle.
translatorRows.different: It is Riesling, not Gewürztraminer — brighter and higher-acid, without Gewürz's lychee, rose, and ginger or its oily, low-acid weight.
translatorRows.phrase: We do not have a Gewürztraminer, but if you want that perfumed, fruity, slightly off-dry style, the Darting Riesling is the closest call — aromatic and a little soft, and great with anything spicy.
flags: No Gewürztraminer or other classic aromatic (Torrontés/Muscat) on the list; Riesling is a fruit-forward/off-dry substitute but differs in aroma (no lychee/rose) and is higher-acid. Confirm Darting sweetness by taste before promising a level.
Donnhoff Feinherb (bottle option) is a Nahe Riesling labelled 'feinherb' (off-dry), i.e. another Riesling, not an aromatic Gewürz-style — a step-up in the SAME Riesling lane.

sources.note: Gewürz = lychee, rose, ginger, off-dry, medium-low/low acidity, full/oily body.

translatorRows.name: Albariño
translatorRows.summary: Two on-menu touchpoints: the 0.0% Neverwine IS Albariño, and Doña Matilde Branco is the dry coastal alternative if they want alcohol.
translatorRows.familiar: Bright, citrusy, saline white with a coastal, seafood-loving snap — exactly the lane Albariño lives in, fresh enough for oysters, crudo, octopus, and shrimp.
translatorRows.different: Doña Matilde is a dry Portuguese Douro white (Arinto, Rabigato, Viosinho, Gouveio), not Albariño, but it shares the citrus-and-saline coastal feel. If the guest is skipping alcohol, our zero-proof Neverwine actually IS Albariño.
translatorRows.phrase: If you love Albariño for that crisp, salty, seafood-friendly style, the Portuguese Doña Matilde is right in that lane — and fun fact, our non-alcoholic Neverwine is literally Albariño if you want the exact grape.
flags: The only Albariño on the menu is the 0.0% non-alcoholic Gallina de Piel Neverwine; there is no alcoholic Albariño by the glass, so Doña Matilde Branco is a coastal-style stand-in, not the same grape.
Doña Matilde Branco is a specific Douro indigenous-grape blend (Arinto, Rabigato, Viosinho, Gouveio), NOT a generic 'blend' — corrected.
Bottle options (Denizot Sancerre = Loire Sauvignon Blanc; Landron Muscadet = Melon de Bourgogne) are crisp coastal/seafood whites but neither is Albariño — honest crisp-white step-ups, not the grape.

sources.note: Albariño from Rías Baixas: high acidity, citrus, salinity, coastal, classic seafood white.
Doña Matilde Branco is Arinto, Viosinho, Gouveio, Rabigato with citrus/balanced acidity.

translatorRows.name: Barolo / Barbaresco
translatorRows.summary: All Nebbiolo: the Ca' del Baio Langhe glass is the same grape, and the Brandini and Fletcher bottles are the step up toward Barolo/Barbaresco weight.
translatorRows.familiar: Same grape — Nebbiolo. Red cherry, rose, and a dry, tea-like tannin grip with high acidity, built for strip steak, lamb, mushrooms, and rich sauces.
translatorRows.different: The Langhe by the glass is a lighter, younger expression than a full Barolo or Barbaresco — the Fletcher Barbaresco is the actual Barbaresco, and the Brandini Langhe Nebbiolo is the richer step up.
translatorRows.phrase: Barolo and Barbaresco are both Nebbiolo, and our Ca' del Baio glass is exactly that grape — same rose, cherry, and grippy tannin. If you want true Barbaresco, the Fletcher bottle is the one.

sources.note: Barolo and Barbaresco are both 100% Nebbiolo from Piedmont; Langhe Nebbiolo is the same grape in a lighter/younger guise.
Nebbiolo: high tannin, high acidity, cherry/rose/tar.

translatorRows.name: Cava
translatorRows.summary: Crisp dry bubbles by the glass (Blue Mountain Brut), with the traditional-method Raventós bottle as the Spanish-sparkling upgrade — honestly noted that Raventós left the Cava DO.
bottleOptions: Raventos i Blanc de Nit Rose
translatorRows.familiar: Dry, crisp traditional-style bubbles with green apple, citrus, and a clean finish — the easy seafood-and-fried-food reset Cava drinkers reach for.
translatorRows.different: The glass is a BC Brut, not Cava. The Raventós bottle is the Spanish move — traditional-method and made mostly from the classic Cava grapes (Xarel·lo, Macabeo, Parellada) plus a touch of Monastrell for the rosé color — though Raventós actually left the Cava DO for its own appellation, so it is even a step above standard Cava.
translatorRows.phrase: For Cava-style bubbles by the glass, the Blue Mountain Brut is dry and crisp in exactly that way — and if you want Spanish sparkling in a bottle, the Raventós is the move, made the same traditional way as Cava.
flags: Raventós i Blanc left DO Cava in Nov 2012 (now labeled Conca del Riu Anoia), so it is not legally 'Cava' even though it is traditional-method Spanish sparkling from Cava grapes.
The menu bottle (Raventós de Nit) is a ROSÉ; the only by-the-glass sparkling is the BC Brut, not Spanish.
MENU LISTS THE GRAPE AS 'MONASTRELL' ONLY, which is misleading: de Nit is ~48% Xarel·lo / ~15% Macabeo / ~32% Parellada + ~5% Monastrell. Record reflects the real blend.
Menu spells the appellation 'Conca del Riu Anioa'; correct spelling is 'Conca del Riu Anoia'.

sources.note: Raventós i Blanc left DO Cava in Nov 2012 to create Conca del Riu Anoia; traditional method, native grapes Macabeo/Xarel·lo/Parellada.
Raventós de Nit Rosé blend is predominantly Xarel·lo/Macabeo/Parellada with ~5% Monastrell for color.

translatorRows.name: Sweet / plush red (Meiomi, Apothic, 19 Crimes)
translatorRows.summary: Expectation-setting case: the cellar has no sweetened reds. Kindly set expectations and steer to the smoothest dry options (St. John Claret / Cerrón Tinto).
translatorRows.familiar: Both are smooth, ripe, dark-fruited reds that feel rich and easy on the palate — the Claret (Merlot-Cabernet) is plush and rounded, and the Cerrón Tinto is dark, full, and fruit-forward.
translatorRows.different: This is the honest part: wines like Meiomi and Apothic are deliberately sweetened with leftover sugar, and we do not pour any sweetened reds. Ours are dry — rich and smooth, but no actual sugar.
translatorRows.phrase: I will be straight with you: we do not have a sweetened red like Meiomi or Apothic — those have added sugar. But if you want a red that drinks rich and smooth, the Claret is plush and soft, and the Cerrón Tinto is dark and full. I can pour a taste so you can feel the difference.
flags: EXPECTATION-SETTING CASE: Meiomi (~19-20 g/L) and Apothic Red (~16 g/L) carry deliberate residual sugar; the cellar has no off-dry/sweet reds, so this row sets expectations honestly rather than claiming a true match. 19 Crimes is comparatively drier but still a plush commercial style.
Menu lists the Napa Merlot bottle simply as 'Whitehall Lane' (Merlot | Napa 2021); corrected bottleOptions to the menu name 'Whitehall Lane'.

sources.note: Meiomi residual sugar reported ~19-20 g/L (lab ~19.4 g/L; website ~20 g/L).
Apothic Red ~16.4 g/L residual sugar — an intentionally sweetened red.

translatorRows.name: Beaujolais Nouveau / light juicy red
translatorRows.summary: For the light, juicy, chillable red lane: the soft Deinhard Pinot Noir by the glass, with the real Gamay (Domaine de Colette) as the bottle.
bottleOptions: Domaine de Colette Coteaux de Colette
translatorRows.familiar: Light-bodied, juicy, low-tannin red with fresh red-berry fruit — the soft, easy, even slightly-chilled style, great with charcuterie, mushrooms, pizza, duck, and trout.
translatorRows.different: Beaujolais Nouveau is young carbonic Gamay with that candied, banana-ish pop; the Deinhard Pinot is drier and more savoury, but the same light, low-tannin, high-acid shape. The Domaine de Colette bottle is proper Beaujolais Gamay.
translatorRows.phrase: If you want that light, juicy, low-tannin red, the Deinhard Pinot is the easy-drinking glass — and for actual Beaujolais Gamay, the Domaine de Colette bottle is the move.
flags: No Beaujolais Nouveau or carbonic-style wine by the glass; the by-the-glass match (Pinot Noir) shares the light/low-tannin shape but not the candied carbonic character. The true Gamay is bottle-only.
Alta Mora Etna Rosso (bottle option) is Nerello Mascalese from Etna — a light, high-acid red in the same SHAPE but not Gamay/carbonic; offered honestly as a light-red alternative.

sources.note: Beaujolais Nouveau: Gamay, carbonic maceration, very low tannin, high acidity, candied/banana fruit.

translatorRows.name: Sancerre
translatorRows.summary: Same crisp, high-acid lane by the glass (Hiedler Löss Grüner), with the Denizot Sancerre bottle as the exact-grape, exact-region answer.
translatorRows.familiar: Crisp, high-acid, mineral white with citrus and a clean, snappy finish — the lean, seafood-and-greens style Sancerre drinkers are after.
translatorRows.different: By the glass it is Grüner Veltliner, not Sauvignon Blanc, so it leans more white-peppery than flinty-grassy. The Denizot Sancerre bottle is the real thing — Loire Sauvignon Blanc.
translatorRows.phrase: If Sancerre is the ask, the Denizot Sancerre is exactly that — Loire Sauvignon Blanc. For a crisp, high-acid glass in the same spirit, I would pour the Hiedler Grüner.
flags: By-the-glass match is Grüner Veltliner (same crisp/high-acid lane, different grape and a bit less grassy); the exact grape/region (Sauvignon Blanc, Sancerre) is bottle-only (Denizot Sancerre).

sources.note: Sancerre is 100% Sauvignon Blanc, cool climate, high acidity, citrus, flinty minerality.

translatorRows.name: Vermentino / coastal Italian white
translatorRows.summary: No Vermentino on the list; the citrusy, saline Doña Matilde Branco is the honest coastal-white stand-in, with crisp Hiedler as a leaner alternative.
translatorRows.familiar: A fresh, citrusy white with a saline, herbal, slightly almond-bitter coastal feel — the seafood-and-antipasti lane Vermentino lives in, great with octopus, olives, shrimp, and lemony pasta.
translatorRows.different: It is a Portuguese Douro white (Arinto, Rabigato, Viosinho, Gouveio), not Vermentino, but it shares that citrus-saline coastal character. For more zip, the Hiedler Grüner is crisper.
translatorRows.phrase: We do not have a Vermentino, but if you want that fresh, citrusy, seaside Italian-white style, the Portuguese Doña Matilde is the closest pour — and if you want maximum crispness, the Grüner is even snappier.
flags: No Vermentino on the menu; Doña Matilde Branco is a coastal-style stand-in, not the same grape or country. Doña Matilde corrected to its named Douro grapes (Arinto, Rabigato, Viosinho, Gouveio).

Bottle options (Cusumano Lucido = Catarratto, Sicily; Ciro Picariello Bru Emm = Falanghina, Campania) are Italian coastal whites in spirit but NOT Vermentino — honest in-cellar Italian-white substitutes.
Menu MISSPELLS both Italian whites: 'Cusomano Lucido' / 'Cataratto' — correct producer/grape are 'Cusumano' and 'Catarratto'.

sources.note: Vermentino: light-medium body, zesty acidity, citrus, almond, salinity, coastal, seafood pairing.
Confirms correct spelling Cusumano Lucido = Catarratto, Sicilia.
